name: Engineering Orchestrator
tag: Keeps engineering projects moving and flags blocked work before deadlines slip.

scenarios.title: Plan a product redesign
scenarios.ask: Plan the bracket redesign for the Line 3 conveyor with {team} engineers, ship in {weeks} weeks, optimizing for {priority}.
steps: Planner
Split the job into {=8 + team * 2} tasks across CAD, load analysis, drawings and the supplier quote.
Scheduler
Assigned owners by skill and current load. Each engineer carries about {=round((8 + team * 2) / team, 1)} tasks.
3D analysis
Load check on the new bracket: peak stress at {=58 + priority * 3}% of yield at twice the rated load.
Watcher
The supplier quote has no owner and blocks day {=round(weeks * 5 * 0.6)}. Flagged to the lead.
followups: What if we lose an engineer mid-project?

The plan re-balances {=round((8 + team * 2) / team)} tasks onto the remaining {=max(1, team - 1)} engineers and the critical path grows by about {=max(1, round(26 / max(1, team - 1) * 2 + 4) - round(26 / team * 2 + 4))} days. You'd see the new dates before approving the change.
Can it talk to our existing tools?
Yes. Tasks sync with Jira, Asana or a shared spreadsheet, and CAD files stay where they are. The Orchestrator only reads what it needs to track progress.
How does it know work is blocked?
Each task has an owner, an input it waits on and a due date. When an input is late or has no owner, the Watcher flags it to the lead with the days of slack left.

scenarios.title: Rescue a slipping project
scenarios.ask: Our {projects} active projects keep slipping. {late}% of tasks are late. Find out why and get us back on track.
steps: Reader
Read {=projects * 34} open tasks across {projects} projects and their handoff history.
Analyst
{=round(late * 0.6)}% of late tasks were waiting on a review that had no named reviewer.
Planner
Proposed a review rota and moved {=round(projects * 1.5)} low-priority tasks out of this month.
Watcher
Set daily checks so any handoff without an owner is flagged within 24 hours.
followups: No. The Watcher sends one short daily note to each lead with only the handoffs that need a decision.
How fast will we see a change?
Most teams see late work drop within two sprints, because the biggest cause, reviews with no owner, is fixed on day one.

scenarios.title: Staff a new contract
scenarios.ask: We won a contract that needs {hours} engineering hours over {months} months. Can our team of {team} take it on?
steps: Capacity
Your team has about {=round(team * months * 140 * 0.55)} free hours over {months} months, after current work.
Planner
Broke the contract into phases and matched skills to each phase.
Risk check
Load peaks in month {=max(1, round(months / 2))}, when two projects overlap.
Recommendation
Compared hiring, contracting and re-sequencing current work.
followups: What if we push the start by a month?
Starting a month later frees about {=round(team * 140 * 0.3)} more hours, because two current projects finish first.
Yes. Add a contractor with their hours and skills, and the Planner gives them the tasks that fit and keeps them off the critical path.
